body:
_Migrated from issue #981, filed 2026-07-18._

## Symptom

A book synced to a Kobo cannot be highlighted/annotated, while other books from the same library work fine. No error is visible anywhere in the UI.

## Root cause (observed on a production instance, v4.1.16)

When a Kobo requests a book that only has an EPUB format, `get_download_link` converts it to KEPUB on demand (`cps/helper.py` ~line 2019). If that conversion fails, the code logs an error and **silently serves the plain EPUB instead** (`book_format = "epub"` fallback). The Kobo then renders the book with its legacy ePub reader, which does not support highlighting or annotations — a permanent, invisible degradation for that book on that device.

The conversion failure in this case was `[Errno 13] Permission denied` writing the `.kepub` into the book folder: the ingest pipeline had created the book directory owned `root:root` while the app runs as `abc` (PUID 1000). 94 paths in the library were root-owned; every one of those books would hit the same failure on first Kobo download.

## Two defects to fix

1. **Ownership**: the ingest/import path can create book directories as root. Book dirs must be created as (or chowned to) the PUID:PGID user. Consider a startup or ingest-time ownership check on the library tree.
2. **Silent degradation**: when on-demand KEPUB conversion fails because the library dir is unwritable, convert into the temp/cache dir and serve that instead of falling back to plain EPUB. If conversion genuinely fails (bad epub), surface the failure (task queue error entry) rather than only a log line — the user-visible effect (no annotations on Kobo) is otherwise undiagnosable.

## Repro

1. `chown root:root` a book folder that has only an EPUB.
2. Sync a Kobo and download the book → device receives plain EPUB, highlighting unavailable.
3. Log shows `On-demand KEPUB conversion failed for book N: [Errno 13] Permission denied`.

## Evidence
- `/config/calibre-web.log` 2026-07-15 01:05: conversion failure for book 535; identical failures for books 533/534 on 2026-07-08.
- After `chown -R abc:abc /calibre-library`, the same endpoint request converted successfully and served a KEPUB with koboSpans.
title: Kobo: failed on-demand KEPUB conversion silently falls back to plain EPUB (book loses highlighting/annotations)
